note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · HUGE AIRY HEAD, HAIRY ANNUAL
tiles.details: Witchgrass is a warm-season fibrous-rooted ANNUAL, not a rhizomatous perennial. Published diffuse panicles ~13–50 cm, often breaking loose when ripe. Actual species panicle panel 3 and hairy-sheath panel 5 are useful, but neither proves a rooted annual or magnified tubercle-based hair origins. Never ID from a detached tumblehead alone.
tiles.short: LOOK HERE FIRST: broad diffuse panicle plus coarse swollen-based hairs on sheath and nodes
tiles.status: ACTUAL HABIT PHOTO — ROOTED ANNUAL/Hair-base MACRO MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · SHORT CILIATE MEMBRANOUS LIGULE
tiles.details: The ligule is a short membrane with marginal cilia; FNA reports cilia ~0.5–1.5 mm, while other floras give ~1–2 mm for the total ligule. Those are different structures and must not be combined. Auricles absent. Current hairy collar photo does not isolate the membrane edge at 1-mm scale.
tiles.short: Expose the TRUE blade–sheath junction, not the long sheath or node hairs

tiles.heading: 03 · SOLITARY TINY MATURE SPIKELETS
tiles.details: Spikelets sit singly at tips of capillary branches; published size ranges vary (Kew ~1.8–2.5 mm, AusGrass ~1.8–3.3 mm). Measure several ripe spikelets with a 1-mm ruler rather than identifying from panicle width or purple color. Existing photo panel 1 shows a real small spikelet but not a Texas same-plant calibrated series.
tiles.short: Individual spikelets ~1.9–4 mm (FNA), not a cluster of awned florets
tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — SAME-PLANT MATURE SPIKELET WITH 1-MM SCALE

tiles.heading: 04 · SHORT LOWER, LONG UPPER GLUME
tiles.details: AusGrass lower glume ~0.9–1.1 mm with 3–5 veins; FNA reports 1–3 veins. Upper glume ~1.8–3.1 mm (FNA) or ~2–3.3 mm (AusGrass), with variable 5–9 veins. These treatment ranges are not measurements of existing images. Photographer-labelled dissection panel 2 teaches glume position but needs locally matched, scaled anatomy.
tiles.short: Lower glume only ~⅓–½ spikelet; upper glume approaches spikelet length

tiles.heading: 05 · SHINY FERTILE LEMMA, NO LONG AWN
tiles.details: Lower sterile lemma commonly ~1.9–3 mm (FNA); upper fertile lemma ~1.5–2 mm in AusGrass, hardened with inrolled margins and enclosed palea. A minute sterile-lemma mucro is possible, but the fertile lemma lacks a projecting long awn. Do not mistake a pointed scale tip for a long awn or infer fine measurements from remote overview panels.
tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma encloses an upper hard shiny fertile floret and palea
tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — MEASURED OPENED SPIKELET AND FERTILE FLORET

tiles.heading: 06 · CHECK ROOTSTOCK BEFORE REMOVAL
tiles.details: Native P. hallii is a glaucous perennial with a tighter, smaller bunch; native P. virgatum is a robust rhizomatous perennial, not defined by one white collar triangle; introduced P. coloratum has a persistent knotty crown. Perennial Dichanthelium rosettes may also confuse sterile shoots. Panel 6 is a DIFFERENT species (P. hallii), never a second witchgrass photo. Match rooted plants and mature spikelets before action.
tiles.short: Separate hairy annual witchgrass from perennial Hall's panicgrass, switchgrass and kleingrass
tiles.status: FIELD COMPARISON — MATCHED ROOTED PLANTS NEEDED

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: WITCHGRASS: Warm-season HAIRY ANNUAL. Find distinct coarse/papillose-based hairs along the sheaths and nodes BELOW an enormous airy irregular many-branch panicle. The ripe ~2–4 mm spikelets sit at tips of extraordinarily slender stems. Confirm annual fibrous rootstock and one measured spikelet with shorter lower glume. Seedhead shape alone will NOT distinguish similarly open Panicum grasses.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: Start with the Matt Lavin whole diffuse-panicle image (gallery panel 3). Identify long slender branches and small distant spikelets without counting glumes from this scale.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: The ligule is a short membrane with marginal cilia; FNA reports cilia ~0.5–1.5 mm, while other floras give ~1–2 mm for the total ligule. Those are different structures and must not be combined. Auricles absent. Current hairy collar photo does not isolate the membrane edge at 1-mm scale.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Spikelets sit singly at tips of capillary branches; published size ranges vary (Kew ~1.8–2.5 mm, AusGrass ~1.8–3.3 mm). Measure several ripe spikelets with a 1-mm ruler rather than identifying from panicle width or purple color. Existing photo panel 1 shows a real small spikelet but not a Texas same-plant calibrated series.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Panicum hallii: Witchgrass is annual, hairy, and has a huge diffuse panicle; Hall's is a perennial glaucous bunchgrass with a smaller stiff-branched panicle. Dichanthelium spp.: Witchgrass is annual and lacks the characteristic spring/fall rosette-grass flowering pattern.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.
